newsitem.title: USA: Executives enter guilty pleas in price-fixing case.
newsitem.headline: Executives enter guilty pleas in price-fixing case.

text.p: Executives of two Japanese companies and one South Korean firm have entered guilty pleas in U.S. District Court here to charges they conspired to fix prices of lysine, a feed additive.

Kanji Mimoto of Ajinomoto Co Inc and Jhom Su Kim of the U.S. subsidiary of Sewon Co Ltd of Korea entered guilty pleas and agreed to pay a fine of $75,000 each. Masaru Yamamoto of Kyowa Hakko Kogyo Co Ltd also pleaded guilty and agreed to a $50,000 fine.
The three executives also agreed to cooperate in the U.S. government's ongoing antitrust case against three former Archer Daniels Midland Co executives.

Michael Andreas, former vice chairman of ADM and son of Chairman Dwayne Andreas, Terrance Wilson, former group vice president of ADM, and Mark Whitacre, who had been president of ADM's BioProducts Division, have each pleaded not guilty to charges of fixing lysine prices.
In October, ADM pleaded guilty to two counts of fixing prices of lysine and agreed to pay $100 million in fines.
